pr_title: config: Make remote-write required for Agent mode
pr_body:
Makes remote-write a requirement for Prometheus running in Agent mode.

Expected behaviors:
* Prometheus will hard fail if started in agent mode without remote-write configuration
* Prometheus is able to run with an invalid remote-write URL. (Will log errors)
* Prometheus won't crash if reload is triggered without remote-write configuration, but won't reload(Will log error)
* Promtool is able to check config files in agent mode if `--agent` flag is passed.

Fixes #9611
pr_comments: I think I just need to add a test for this and it should be good to go 🙂

Thank you.

I think we should have actionnable error messages:

`field alerting not allowed in agent mode`
`field remote_read not allowed in agent mode`
`field rule_files is not allowed in agent mode`

and

`at least one remote_write target must be specified in agent mode`

I think I've addressed everything! Thanks for the review, by the way. 

This is the first time I'm getting my head around the agent so your hints regarding all other requirements besides the remote-write were very much appreciated :)

issue_context.title: Agent: Add validation that fails agent if no remote write is configured.
comments: That's interesting. Should we error or should we warn? What should we do if remote write is removed while the agent is running?

> That's interesting. Should we error or should we warn? What should we do if remote write is removed while the agent is running?

It should probably fail validation and not make any runtime changes to remote_write unless there's at least one in the file.

I can see it being a warning too, though: in the worst case you have a WAL that keeps stale series in it up to the max WAL time before new GCs will clean them up.

Is there any use-case for an agent without a remote-write?

If there isn't then I think the most reasonable approach would be a hard-fail for the agent 🤔

Letting it run may misguide users that everything is working as expected

The only use case I've really been able to identify is doing cardinality analysis on the WAL without having to persist metrics. But there's still reasonable workarounds to give you similar things: temporary Prometheus server that you spin down later, or a fake remote_write endpoint, etc. 

Bringing up the lack of a use case is a really good point, and I'm on the side of having the validation hard-reject configs without any remote_writes. That restriction can always be lifted if a nice use case shows up.

review_comments: We can also error if rule_files or alerting is set.
